newsitem.title: CANADA: Beatrice to reorganize under protection laws.
newsitem.headline: Beatrice to reorganize under protection laws.

text.p: Privately held Beatrice Foods Inc said on Wednesday it filed a reorganization plan under Canadian creditor protection laws and would ask holders of its US$150 million series of debentures to approve the plan.
The food processor said it filed a plan under the Canada Business Corporations Act and the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act.
Beatrice said it will convert its subordinated debt into common equity to significantly reduce debt and put the company into new ownership.
Beatrice called noteholders to meet on October 18 in Toronto but the plan has been endorsed by a steering committee of holders who hold more than 75 percent of the debentures, it said.
"No creditors of the company other than the noteholders are being compromised or will vote on the plan," it added.

"With the implementation of this plan, the new Beatrice will have less than C$125 million in debt, compared with in excess of C$400 million prior to the recapitalization," said chief executive officer Brent Ballantyne in a statement.
Beatrice owns dairy, cheese and bakery plants.

"Under the plan, approximately C$45 million of new equity will be raised through a fully backstopped rights offering. The existing shareholder will receive warrants entitling it to purchase 600,000 shares of Beatrice at an exercise price ranging from C$30 to C$40 over a term of five years," it said.

A major Canadian chartered bank agreed to give Beatrice a new term facility. With all the proceeds, "...outstanding indebtedness on the Company's existing senior term and operating loan will be fully repaid," the firm said.
